newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: DUTCH NEDCAR PLANS NIGHTSHIFTS TO RAISE OUTPUT.
newsitem.headline: DUTCH NEDCAR PLANS NIGHTSHIFTS TO RAISE OUTPUT.

text.p: Nedcar, a joint venture between Volvo Car, Mitsubishi Motors Corp and the Dutch government, requested on Wednesday a licence from the Dutch ministry of social affairs to introduce nightshifts.

Nedcar spokesman Fokko Haanstra said the licence was of vital importance for the car maker as it would give Nedcar the opportunity to reach its production target of 280,000 cars a year by 1998, up from a planned output of 145,000 in 1996.
"We need to increase our annual production hours to 5,000 from 4,000," Haanstra said, adding the firm had to meet demands for higher production levels from its shareholders.

In August Nedcar said it was failing to meet this year's output targets. Mitsubishi Motors Europe president K. Sato told a Dutch newspaper in August the company wanted to step up its production of vehicles in Europe and it might have to consider producing cars at alternative sites unless Nedcar raised output.
Nedcar, based in the southern Dutch town of Born, said it was hoping to increase the production hours by one quarter by the end of this year or early 1997.
The Nedcar-spokesman said the introduction of nightshifts would demand only a small investment.
